source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rural.evidence: No rural revenue % disclosed; company is instead expanding into tier-2 cities (Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, upcoming Guwahati/Noida) which management frames as future 'medical hubs' rather than rural markets: 'there's a lot of skepticism about why are you going to tier-2... we do believe that the Lucknow-Kanpur region will also become a medical hub.'

govt_capex.evidence: 'We enrolled the Ayushman Bharat and CGHS and other schemes, enabling us to serve a broader patient population.' Payer mix is ~82% cash+TPA group-wide (implying ~18% institutional/PPP/scheme business, higher in Patna/Lucknow). Also obtained government-allocated land in Guwahati, Assam under the state's 'Invest in Assam' initiative for a 400-bed hospital.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ~INR 4,000 crore capex earmarked over 3-4 years 'funded through a combination of internal approvals and the debt financing'; company ended FY25 with a net cash surplus of INR 8,123 million, indicating currently low leverage. No floating-rate % disclosed in the transcript.

inr_exposure.evidence: International patient revenue was INR 2,086 million (~6% of total revenue) in FY25, up 8% YoY. Post the MHPL(Lucknow)-GHL merger, 'export benefits under EPCG scheme will now be available to Lucknow against the Forex earnings of the GHL.'

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary: 'Leading Indian CDMOs like Syngene, Neuland Labs, and Divi's Laboratories are reporting a significant increase in RFQs from global pharmaceutical giants looking to de-risk their supply chains, and are successfully converting these inquiries into concrete pilot projects and commercial contracts.' Divi's has earmarked aggressive capex (~₹1,000-2,000 crore over two years) explicitly framed around the China+1 driven ~$20bn API off-patent opportunity (FY23-25).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Divi's is widely reported as a near debt-free company; no specific floating-rate liability % located in available sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company 'enters hedging transactions as and when required' and manages currency risk 'by having a better geographic balance in revenue mix and ensuring a foreign currency match between liabilities and earnings'; also has fixed-exchange-rate contracts with major clients where FX fluctuation risk is shared.
inr_exposure.evidence: Net foreign currency exposure was ₹1,521 crore as of March 31, 2024, vs ₹1,241 crore a year earlier. Exports (predominantly USD/EUR invoiced) are ~88-90% of revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories is cited among beneficiaries of India's PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs (KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs), which offers 10-20% incentive on incremental sales of qualified APIs; specific revenue/incentive amount not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/diversification framing found; company instead discusses generic API supply-chain risk mitigation ('expanding internal API capacity, entering toll-manufacturing/JV agreements, long-term purchase agreements... to lower dependence on constrained intermediates') and organic capex (₹290.7 crore in Q3FY25) to reduce supplier bargaining power.

inr_exposure.evidence: 'US Formulation business generated revenue of Rs 2,409.6 crore, up 30.8% YoY, and accounted for 47% of consolidated revenues' (Q3 FY25). India Formulations grew at a 21.8% CAGR FY23-25 vs. US Formulations at 31.0% CAGR, suggesting a rising USD-revenue share over the period.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed disclosure found of Zydus as an approved PLI beneficiary (bulk drugs or medical devices) in sources reviewed, despite the company's API and newly-launched medical devices (interventional cardiology stents, via partnership with Braile Biomedica) businesses potentially qualifying.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 Q4 results framed the company as 'the world's largest downstream steel player outside China' (3.1 million tons sales volume) — a scale/market-position claim rather than an explicit customer-diversification-from-China narrative tied to revenue growth.

rural.evidence: Dated data point: 'nearly 60% of FY21 revenue' came from tier-2/rural areas (pandemic-era reverse migration); company's 'Chaukhat' door-frame product directly targets PMAY-Gramin rural housing construction; distribution network of 800+ distributors across 300+ towns. No current FY25 rural revenue % located.

govt_capex.evidence: 'PMAY-Gramin has been extended to FY29, targeting 2 crore additional rural houses, and PMAY-Urban 2.0 targets 1 crore urban houses over five years. The programmes require structural tubes for roofing supports and door frames.' Company serves 'urban infrastructure and real estate' as a core end-market alongside rural housing.

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 capacity expansion from 3.6MT to 5MT (~₹600 crore capex) was 'funded fully by internal accruals,' suggesting limited reliance on floating-rate debt for that program.

inr_exposure.evidence: Predominantly domestic-focused; company exports to ~20-30 countries but export share of revenue was not disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (₹6,322 crore outlay) covers coated/plated steel, high-strength steel, specialty rails, alloy steel & wires, and electrical steel; no confirmed disclosure found that APL Apollo (structural/GI steel tubes) is a named beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'Rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits NFIL's export-led business.' Specialty and CRAMS/CDMO segments now contribute over 60% of revenue, cited as driving structural margin improvement alongside this trend.

rate_sensitive.evidence: CARE Ratings noted net debt-to-equity of ~0.01x, with 'Wave-2' capacity expansion 'funded through internal accruals' — indicating minimal reliance on floating-rate borrowings.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not crude-oil dependent. Primary raw materials are fluorspar, chloroform and sulphur — 'fluorspar alone contributing over 40% of the overall raw material cost' and is largely imported, with China controlling a large share of global fluorspar supply (mitigated via long-term contracts with South African miners).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share of revenue fluctuated across FY25 quarters: 57% in Q1 FY25 (43% domestic) vs. 77% in Q4 FY25, indicating substantial and growing foreign-currency (largely USD) revenue exposure. No specific full-year figure or hedging % disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilisers has been developing a PLI scheme for the specialty chemicals sector; no confirmed disclosure found that Navin Fluorine is an approved beneficiary as of FY25.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports accounted for 10.63% of the total turnover, with ferro alloys and stainless steel being the major export products (no explicit China+1/diversification framing found).

govt_capex.evidence: Ongoing government-driven infrastructure expansion in India (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing) is expected to fuel robust demand for steel, stainless steel, and aluminium products, providing a long-term tailwind for Shyam Metalics' volume growth; TMT bars/wire rods are core inputs to construction and infrastructure projects.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Debt-to-equity of ~0.08x with a net cash position of ~₹378 crore; company funds capex mainly through internal accruals and approaches banks only for working capital, indicating low rate sensitivity overall.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (ferro alloys, stainless steel, DI pipes) accounted for ~10.6% of total turnover.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics Flat Products has been selected under the PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel, investing in high-strength automotive steel and CRGO electrical steel under the PLI ambit, alongside Tata Steel, JSW Steel, JSPL, AM/NS India, SAIL.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India's operations are world-class, offering productivity and labor arbitrage advantages, and the company is export-ready, with global ABB divisions deciding on expansion/export allocation based on market needs (no explicit China+1 framing).

govt_capex.evidence: Diversified presence across 23 market segments positions ABB India to benefit from sustained investment in infrastructure, rail, grid modernization and renewables; secured Mumbai Metro traction orders (18 six-car trainsets Line 6, 22 six-car trainsets Line 5) and completed Kolkata Metro upgrades; order pipeline strong across power, metro, T&D, railways. Government Railways capex allocation of ~₹2,62,200 crore and overall public capex of ₹12.2 lakh crore cited as tailwinds.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India carries net cash (~₹51.9b net cash vs ~₹732m debt as of mid-2025) with debt-to-equity near 0.7%, indicating minimal exposure to rate movements.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for only ~10% of ABB India's business mix; company was asked about roadmap to raise exports over 3-5 years.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports appear minimal relative to revenue (Q1 FY27 export revenue of ~₹50 crore was said to nearly match the entire prior year's export total, against FY25 revenue of ~₹5,536 crore); no diversification/export narrative found.

rural.evidence: Industry-level driver: rural electrification under the Saubhagya Scheme and smart-grid projects are propelling uptake of LT/HT power cables, with the next phase targeting the final 12 million unelectrified rural homes; Finolex Cables cited as a key beneficiary of India's infrastructure/rural electrification push (third-party market commentary, not company-disclosed %).

govt_capex.evidence: Market commentary: full railway network electrification, rural electrification schemes, BharatNet optical fibre rollout and smart city projects cited as demand drivers for Finolex's cable business.

crude_exposure.evidence: Finolex Cables' competitive edge comes from backward integration in copper and PVC; PVC resin is a crude-oil derivative input alongside copper, but no quantified raw-material % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue appears to be a small single-digit share of total sales (see China+1 evidence above); no hedging policy disclosure located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Anthem Biosciences is distinguished by its 'China-plus-one' strategy, having built a supply chain with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials; global pharma companies are diversifying away from China due to geopolitical risk, with Anthem positioned as a key beneficiary/alternative — management stated it is 'now the second source for many Chinese products,' with plans to become the first choice for new ones.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed 85% of revenue from operations for FY2025-26, with the company serving customers across 50 countries — a highly export-oriented, USD-linked revenue model as a global CRDMO serving international pharma/biotech clients.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch aims to double its exports from India by 2030, leveraging the country's cost-effective and competitive industrial base — especially in auto components; current exports are about 9-10% of production (Guruprasad Mudlapur interview, July 2025). Export-growth ambition is framed around India's cost/manufacturing competitiveness rather than an explicit 'China+1' label.

rural.evidence: In the tractor and two-wheeler segments, rural purchasing power driven by agricultural income is a primary demand driver; tractor business projected to hit records supported by strong rural sentiment, GST norms and state subsidies; two-wheeler business grew 63.4% YoY in FY2025-26 aided by OBD2-norm-driven sensor sales.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw materials required for manufacturing include steel, plastic, rubber, LPG and CNG — plastic/rubber components and LPG/CNG inputs carry direct crude-oil/gas price linkage, though no quantified raw-material % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are about 9-10% of production with a stated plan to double this by 2030.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch is among the listed beneficiaries of the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components, alongside Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Tata Autocomp, Mitsubishi Electric, Toyota Kirloskar, Motherson Sumi and Lucas-TVS.

china_plus_one.evidence: GHFL exports to 90+ countries with 5,000+ tinters; ~77% of FY25 revenue came from exports and ~80% from value-added films, but no explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing was found in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Major raw materials like PTA & MEG come from crude oil, whose prices are volatile; Garware mitigates this with forward contracts and long-term agreements.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Forward contracts and long-term agreements used to mitigate crude-oil-linked raw material (PTA/MEG) price volatility; no explicit revenue-hedging % disclosed in sources found.
inr_exposure.evidence: 77% of FY2025 revenue came from exports; North America alone was cited as accounting for about 55% of total sales.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of GSK Pharmaceuticals Ltd (India) participating in the pharma/API PLI schemes; company is primarily a domestic branded-formulations and vaccines marketer (FY24-25 revenue from operations ~Rs 3,723 crore) rather than a bulk-drug/API manufacturer, which are the main PLI beneficiary categories.

rural.evidence: Consumption in Tier-2/3/4 cities as well as rural areas could outpace that of urban cities, which would be beneficial for United Spirits considering its well-entrenched manufacturing and distribution footprint across India.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material cost driver is Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA, ~40% of raw material costs), sourced from sugarcane molasses and grains rather than crude oil/petroleum derivatives.

inr_exposure.evidence: United Spirits generates the large majority of its revenue domestically within India (Prestige & Above ~89% of net sales, Popular ~10-11%); no material export revenue percentage was disclosed in sources found.

china_plus_one.evidence: "The dumping of steel into India has resulted in excess availability which continues to dent market sentiments and remains a serious threat to the domestic steel industry" — JSW frames Chinese steel exports as a competitive threat to its home market, not as a China+1 diversification tailwind.

govt_capex.evidence: Company cites government infrastructure-led initiatives, renewable energy, automotive, household appliances and affordable housing as major demand drivers; approved capex plan of ~Rs 61,863 crore over three years for capacity/downstream expansion; high-margin Value-Added Special Products (VASP) segment was 62% of sales (ex-JVML) in FY25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: As of March 31, 2025, JSW Steel's debt mix was 37% fixed-rate bonds/debentures and 63% floating-rate loans; company uses interest rate swaps to manage USD floating-rate exposure and maintains a policy of balancing fixed/floating borrowings.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are iron ore and coking coal, not crude oil/petroleum derivatives; no crude-oil framing of raw material risk found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Hedging policy covers the revenue account fully on a gross basis and the next one year's debt service obligations; company maintains a policy of hedging up to 25% of consumption exposure. As of March 31, 2025, 56% of total debt was foreign-currency denominated vs 44% INR.
inr_exposure.evidence: "JSW Steel uses derivative financial instruments to hedge the foreign currency risk arising on account of its revenue and debt portfolio"

pli_scheme.evidence: JSW Steel is among the top steel companies selected under the government's PLI scheme for specialty steel, having submitted applications across six specialty steel product categories.

china_plus_one.evidence: "The fast growing global EV market is looking to diversify supply chains and mitigate risk stemming from dependency on limited and unreliable sources" — noting 95% of world rare-earth metals and 75% of neodymium magnets come from China; Sona developed magnet-less motor technology (with IRP Nexus Group, Israel) to reduce this dependency, and the company serves 7 of the top 10 global carmakers while explicitly pursuing diversification 'across products, customers, and geographies' to reduce concentration risk. BEV revenue was 38% higher YoY, accounting for 36% of FY25 annual revenue.

inr_exposure.evidence: Geographic revenue reported as ~41% India, ~30% North America, ~24% Europe (most recent quarterly disclosure available, not confirmed as exact full-FY25 annual split); company operates 12 plants across India, USA, Mexico and China providing partial natural hedge.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first auto component supplier to receive Auto PLI certification (hub wheel drive motor for e-two-wheelers) and has since received certification for three additional EV traction motor products (two for e-three-wheelers, one for e-two-wheelers) under India's Production-Linked Incentive scheme for advanced automotive technology.

govt_capex.evidence: Coforge has a public-enterprises/government vertical projected to grow from $131M to ~$250M by 2030, but this is public-sector IT spend, not infrastructure capex.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Coforge purchases forward foreign exchange contracts (typically 1-12 month maturities) to hedge INR-USD, INR-GBP, INR-EUR exposure on expected cash flows and receivables; used as economic hedges, mostly qualifying for hedge accounting.
inr_exposure.evidence: "Coforge has sought to reduce the effect of Indian Rupee-US Dollar, Indian Rupee-Pound Sterling, Indian Rupee-Euro and certain other local currency exchange rate fluctuations... by purchasing forward foreign exchange contracts."

china_plus_one.evidence: "Continued policy thrust towards Make in India, Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, electric mobility, localisation of advanced automotive technologies and infrastructure development is expected to create significant long-term opportunities for the Indian automotive and auto component industry." Aftermarket/exports business expanded across 6 export regions (SAARC, ASEAN, EU, LATAM, MENA, Africa); seating division crossed ₹200 crore exports in FY24.

rural.evidence: Uno Minda's portfolio is split roughly PV (~47%) and 2W (~45%) by vehicle segment; 2-wheelers are a common proxy for rural/semi-urban demand in India, but no explicit rural revenue % is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported at ~1.2x EBITDA with EBIT covering interest ~8.6x; company also has fixed-coupon NCDs outstanding (e.g., 7.11% and 7.85% series), but no floating-rate liability % disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company cites commodity cost pressure from aluminium, steel and plastics (plastics/rubber being crude derivatives), but no quantified % of raw material basket tied to crude/petrochemicals was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: "PLI Scheme: Uno Minda, Voltas among 18 new firms selected for AC, LED light components" (3rd round of White Goods PLI). Sector commentary also names Uno Minda among auto-component makers positioned around the Auto PLI/Component Champion scheme, though it is not on the primary named Component Champion beneficiary list (Maruti, Hero, Tata Autocomp, Motherson, Bosch, Lucas-TVS) found in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Netweb is an "Indian origin OEM" building HPC/AI/server systems "under the 'Make in India' initiative," and holds Class-I local-supplier status that reserves the entire central government/PSU/defence server market (est. ₹6,000-8,000 crore annually) for domestic manufacturers over imported (largely foreign/Chinese-supply-chain) servers; won ~₹450 crore in Tranche-1 IndiaAI Mission orders (Tranche-2 ~₹1,200 crore) directly tied to this import-substitution policy.

govt_capex.evidence: Class-I supplier status reserves the entire central government, PSU and defence server addressable market (~₹6,000-8,000 crore/year) for Netweb and similar local suppliers; also won IndiaAI Mission tranche orders (~₹450 crore Tranche-1, ~₹1,200 crore Tranche-2 estimated across consortia).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported a net cash-positive position (~₹1,621 million) at FY25 year-end, implying limited floating-rate debt exposure, though no explicit % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: "exports remaining around 5% (as of FY26)... export revenue contribution stood at 9% in Q3 FY25" — company is overwhelmingly domestic-revenue focused.

pli_scheme.evidence: "Netweb Technologies receives incentive of Rs 5.93 cr under PLI scheme 2.0 for IT hardware" for the period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024; company is stated to be eligible under both IT Hardware PLI and Telecom & Networking PLI schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company is described as "the first company in India (outside China) to develop electrolyte additives on a commercial scale," and positioned as competing directly with Chinese manufacturers in specialty chemicals/pharma intermediates via import substitution; USFDA and PMDA-approved facilities serve 160+ customers across 25+ countries.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Reported "nil term debt repayment obligations" and a net cash position (₹2.25 billion cash vs ₹355.96 million debt), indicating minimal debt/rate sensitivity.

crude_exposure.evidence: Pharma intermediates and specialty chemicals are typically petrochemical-feedstock-derived industry-wide, but no company-specific % of raw material tied to crude derivatives was found in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: "Total exports represented 74% of total revenue in FY25"; "exports accounted for nearly 76% of revenues in Q2 FY26."

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found naming Acutaas Chemicals/Ami Organics as an approved beneficiary under the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs/KSM-API (48 approved projects nationally) despite targeted search; company's own commentary emphasizes CDMO/custom-synthesis growth rather than PLI incentives.

rural.evidence: "Radico's strength lies in its ability to adapt: launching new-age, premium products while continuing to dominate in semi-urban and rural segments with trusted value brands"; pan-India network reaching 60,000-100,000+ retail outlets with emphasis on semi-urban/rural penetration. No explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: "Surging crude oil prices and a weaker rupee are increasing import costs for packaging and other inputs"; industry-wide cost hikes cited: glass bottles up ~20%, paper cartons ~100%, logistics costs up ~10%. Key raw materials are grain, ENA and glass, with glass/packaging costs linked to crude/energy prices.

inr_exposure.evidence: "Radico Khaitan derives 5% to 6% of sales volumes and 9% to 10% of revenue from exports" across 100+ countries.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to the alco-beverage sector; no evidence found of Radico being a PLI beneficiary.
